01 / The challenge

Every journey has a story.
Risk is part of it.

Newly licensed drivers face changing roads, speed environments and intersections. DriveXa brings the relevant context into view before a trip begins.

What if a young driver could understand the road ahead before reaching a difficult section?

DriveXa analyses a planned journey using factors such as historical crash exposure, speed environments and road conditions. It identifies road segments that may require extra attention and explains the contributing factors in plain language.

WHO

Melbourne drivers aged 18–25, especially newly licensed and early independent drivers.

WHERE

Urban and metropolitan journeys, including unfamiliar higher-speed roads, complex intersections and changing conditions.

WHY

Limited experience can make it harder to judge how a road environment changes the level of attention required.

HOW

Simple, explainable pre-drive information highlights higher-attention segments and the reasons behind them.

S

Sally

Young Victorian driver · persona

Her goal

Feel prepared on unfamiliar roads; recognise higher-risk sections early and understand why extra attention may be needed.

Her frustration

  • Sudden changes can be hard to anticipate.
  • Navigation rarely explains road risk.
  • Limited experience makes surprises harder to handle.
02 / Our approach

Built on evidence.
Improved by feedback.

Six connected practices shaped the prototype and kept design, data and delivery aligned.

01 / ITERATE

Iterative development

Progress through planned releases: first establish journey planning and relative risk, then refine clarity, safety and usability.

02 / ORGANISE

Kanban project management

Use LeanKit to organise epics, user stories, acceptance criteria and tasks, with clear ownership and progress tracking.

03 / VALIDATE

Requirements-driven delivery

Check the prototype and implementation against agreed user stories and acceptance criteria throughout each iteration.

04 / LISTEN

Feedback-driven refinement

Turn mentor, tutor, peer and user feedback into changes in project scope and product experience.

05 / EXPLAIN

Evidence-based design

Use validated road-safety information and transparent baseline rules, with contributing factors and clear data limitations.

06 / CONNECT

Interdisciplinary integration

Connect AI, BIS, DS and IT work through shared prototypes, data models, database and API requirements.

Our process kept the project focused on useful pre-drive awareness.PLAN → BUILD → TEST → REFINE
03 / Development

Two iterations.
One clearer journey.

From a core risk-awareness journey to a more explainable, safety-aware and user-friendly experience.

01

Establish the core.

The first iteration enabled users to plan a journey, view its sections and understand which parts may demand more attention.

It introduced low, medium and high attention levels with initial explanations based on relevant road-risk factors.

Iteration 1 completed
01 / PLANJourney input and overview
02 / SEEInteractive route and road sections
03 / ASSESSRelative attention classification
04 / UNDERSTANDInitial risk explanations and journey summary

LeanKit organised the iteration around journey planning, baseline young-driver risk assessment and basic risk explanations.

02

Make risk meaningful.

The second iteration moved beyond basic risk identification to show more clearly where attention is needed, why it matters and what users can do before driving.

Feedback shaped stronger safety prompts, easier journey setup and better system responses.

Iteration 2 completed
01 / CLARIFYDetailed segment risk factors and explanations
02 / CONTEXTJourney time and speed-zone changes
03 / SUPPORTPractical driving tips for higher-risk sections
04 / IMPROVEMy Location, recent locations and clearer feedback
05 / SAFETYPre-drive notice and user acknowledgement
06 / ACCESSProtected prototype entry

LeanKit tracked detailed risk profiles, context-aware factors and journey experience improvements.

Product experience

Plan. Review. Understand.

DriveXa shows a recommended route and its journey segments, then presents relative risk levels, contributing factors and practical advice. The second iteration added clearer explanations, loading feedback, a safety reminder and faster journey setup.
